definitions.explanation: The act or place of crossing over something, such as a river, road, or body of water.
A convenient connection or opportunity, especially in the expression 渡りに船 (a boat at the crossing — a fortunate opportunity arriving at just the right moment).

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}の{渡|わた}りは{危険|きけん}だ。
{渡|わた}り{鳥|どり}が{南|みなみ}へ{飛|と}んでいく{季節|きせつ}になった。
examples.english: The season has come for migratory birds to fly south.

examples.japanese: この{橋|はし}は{昔|むかし}から{渡|わた}りの{要所|ようしょ}として{使|つか}われてきた。
examples.english: This bridge has been used as an important crossing point since ancient times.

examples.japanese: {渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}とはこのことだ。
examples.english: This is exactly what they mean by 'a boat at the crossing.'

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}したいと{思|おも}っていたら、{友人|ゆうじん}が{部屋|へや}を{紹介|しょうかい}してくれて、{渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}だった。
examples.english: I was wanting to move, and then a friend introduced me to an apartment — it was perfect timing.

examples.japanese: {転職|てんしょく}を{考|かんが}えていた{矢先|やさき}にスカウトの{電話|でんわ}があり、まさに{渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}だった。
examples.english: Just when I was thinking about changing jobs, I got a scouting call — it was truly a godsend.

notes:
USAGE:
The noun form of the verb {渡|わた}る (to cross). Used in compounds and set expressions.

KEY EXPRESSION:
{渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}: literally "a boat at the crossing" — describes a fortunate opportunity that appears at exactly the right moment. Similar to the English "just what the doctor ordered" or "a godsend."

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {渡|わた}り{鳥|どり}: migratory bird
- {渡|わた}り{廊下|ろうか}: covered walkway connecting buildings
- {渡|わた}り{歩|ある}く: to wander from place to place
- {渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}: a fortunate coincidence
